A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACE diffusion-steering work. Their complete main texts and appendices A–F are readable, and equations, tables, figures, and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original checkerboard simulations, molecular scaffold-decoration experiments, and COCO-MIG image-generation results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic, scaffold-decoration, fragment-linking, and image-generation results, alongside additional sensitivity and comparison experiments.

M1.justification: The weighted Feynman–Kac sampler and Algorithms 1–2 remain essentially unchanged. v2 extends the quadratic bump with a piecewise-linear component, specifies corrections across covering coordinate subsets, and introduces ACE-lite without resampling. These are procedural extensions within the retained ACE framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual pocket-conditioned fragment-linking evaluation on 66 fragment pairs; v1 only formulated this task and left empirical validation to future work. Scaffold evaluation replaces the deliberately weak-binding and model-generated CrossDock subsets with eligible CrossDocked test ligands. Checkerboard and COCO-MIG task coverage remains.

E2.justification: DiffDec disappears from the scaffold comparison, while Delete and AutoFragDiff remain. v2 adds evaluated heuristic time-varying guidance schedules, the schedule-aligned FKC-TRP comparator, and FFLOM for fragment linking (Appendices C.3, E.6, and E.2). These substantially expand the alternatives tested.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 changes molecular evaluation to 76 eligible test pairs and batch size 5 instead of 10. It adds QED, SA, and Lipinski metrics and revises docking aggregation, replacing standalone validity reporting. New parameter-grid and alignment protocols are specified. Image-runtime evaluation now reports A100 hardware for ACE/FKC instead of A6000.

E4.justification: v2 adds joint B1/B2 sensitivity grids, heuristic guidance-schedule controls, schedule-alignment analysis, and ACE-lite efficiency/performance comparisons. These test correction strength, whether time variation alone suffices, and resampling tradeoffs. The earlier ESS and single-bump analyses are retained, partly relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 adds molecular docking standard deviations across generated molecules and specifies three seeds for new scaffold-schedule comparisons and one for fragment linking. The main scaffold description omits v1's explicit two-seed averaging statement; this does not establish a reduction in runs. Five-seed synthetic uncertainty reporting remains.

E6.justification: Molecular Tables 3–4 are replaced: ACE at guidance 1.4 reports mean Vina −7.10 on v2's test cohort, versus −5.37 on v1's CrossDock-Weak cohort, which is not a comparable-setting gain. v2 adds fragment-linking, alignment, sensitivity, and ACE-lite results and revises image runtime/memory values. Original checkerboard Table 2 survives as Table C.2; COCO-MIG accuracy values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds the zero-criterion boundary counterexample, an explicit finite-score/wrong-endpoint example, and a partial-support correction corollary. It reformulates the bump theorem around a truncated sampling horizon and revises Proposition E.1's tail bounds and proof. The concentration result already existed in v1; its revision, rather than promotion into the main text, constitutes theoretical change.

C1.justification: The central collapse diagnosis and ACE contribution remain. v2 qualifies the earlier claim of predicting collapse exactly as a sharp sufficient criterion with an ambiguous zero boundary, and states the constructive guarantee up to the final sampling timestep. The headline synthetic error-reduction claim changes from over 5× to approximately 4×.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes endpoint Bayesian factorization from intermediate transport paths, attributes schedule-alignment failures to nonuniform temporal evolution, and interprets the new guidance controls as evidence for validity-preserving correction. It adds ACE-lite's speed-versus-bias tradeoff and clarifies that ACE cannot repair inaccurate or semantically misaligned experts.

D1.justification: v2 adds project/code access information and a reproducibility statement. It documents molecular atom-count/type restrictions, pretrained-model data provenance, bond reconstruction, guidance-specific B2 values, baseline settings, and fragment-linking implementation. Hardware and memory disclosures are also revised. Newly documented details do not establish that every underlying procedure changed.

R1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D substantially expand positioning against prior time-dependent guidance, including Wang et al. (2024b) and Jin et al. (2026), distinguishing path-validity correction from empirical guidance schedules. Additional discussion covers time reparameterization, discrete/RL steering, and fragment-linking research. Bibliographic updates to retained works are separate presentation changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method narrative, and discussion are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces a three-step method overview, a standalone related-work section, scope/limitations discussion, and reproducibility and impact statements. Appendix organization and author information also change, beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, redraws the overview, replaces the main molecular illustration, restructures molecular tables, and adds parameter-grid, guidance-comparison, and runtime displays. Existing material is also relocated: v1 Figure 6 becomes Figure C.4, while the concentration illustration moves from the appendix into the main text.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's limited molecular validation through a broader test cohort, actual fragment-linking experiments, and controls comparing alternative guidance and schedule alignment. Boundary-case analysis, the revised tail proof, and implementation/code disclosures improve rigor and reproducibility. These gains outweigh removal of DiffDec and standalone validity reporting, although single-seed fragment evaluation, incomplete main molecular seed reporting, and some text/table inconsistencies remain.
